candidates.label: Cenchreae archaeological site
candidates.support: Cenchreae, per Wikidata, was 'the eastern port town of ancient Corinth' on the Saronic Gulf, distinct from other ancient places of the same name; Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates for the site agree closely.

summary.text: Cenchreae was Corinth's eastern harbor on the Saronic Gulf. Acts records that Paul had his hair cut off there under a vow before sailing for Syria, and Paul's letter to the Romans commends Phoebe as a servant of the church at Cenchreae.

scripture.textWEB: Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers, and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the assembly that is at Cenchreae,

Roman province of Achaia (ruler: Senate, proconsul (restored by the emperor Claudius))

politicalHistory.note: The Roman biographer Suetonius: on his departure from Greece, the emperor Nero "presented the entire province with freedom."

The Roman biographer Suetonius records that the emperor Vespasian "made provinces of Achaia, Lycia, Rhodes, Byzantium and Samos, taking away their freedom," but gives no year for this, so the status here is shown as unclear from Vespasian's first full year as emperor until his death in 79, when it is a province again.
